1 عَبِقَ بِهِ الطِّيبُ , [aor.
عَبَقَ ,] inf. n. عَبَقٌ (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and عَبَاقِيَةٌ (S, O, K) and عَبَاقَةٌ, (O, K,) The perfume clung to him, or it, (S, Mgh, O, K, TA,) and remained; and so عَسِقَ به; (TA;) and the odour of the perfume clung to him, or it: (Mgh:) or the odour of the perfume was, or became, perceptible in his garment or his person: and it is said to relate only to fragrant odour. (Msb.) ―
-b2- And in like manner one says of a garment, عَبِقَ بِالجِسْمِ [It clung to the body]. (TA.) And عَبِقَ الشَّىْءُ بِغَيْرِهِ The thing clave, or kept, to another. (Msb.) And عَبِقَ الشَّىْءُ بِقَلْبِى (tropical:) The thing stuck to my heart. (TA.) And عَبِقَ بِالمَكَانِ He remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in the place. (O, K.) And عَبِقَ بِهِ (tropical:) He became attached to him, or it. (O, K, TA.) [See also رَصِعَ بِالطِّيبِ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
